data.name: Get open GitHub issues
data.evaluateGuide:
Retrieves open issues for a specified GitHub repository, enabling agents to review currently active work items. The response may also include pull requests.
Use for: monitor open issues, find unassigned work, review repository activity
Not supported: closed-issue retrieval, issue creation, issue comments, pull-request listing

data.name: List repository issues
data.description:
List repository issues
List issues in a repository. Only open issues will be listed.

[!NOTE]
  GitHub's REST API considers every pull request an issue, but not every issue is a pull request. For this reason, "Issues" endpoints may return both issues and pull requests in the response. You can identify pull requests by the pull_request key. Be aware that the id of a pull request returned from "Issues" endpoints will be an issue id. To find out the pull request id, use the "List pull requests" endpoint.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "Media types."

application/vnd.github.raw+json: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include body. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
application/vnd.github.text+json: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include body_text.
application/vnd.github.html+json: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include body_html.
application/vnd.github.full+json: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include body, body_text, and body_html.

Parameters
| Name | In | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| owner | path | Yes | The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive. |
| repo | path | Yes | The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive. |
| milestone | query | No | If an integer is passed, it should refer to a milestone by its number field. If the string * is passed, issues wit |
| state | query | No | Indicates the state of the issues to return. |
| assignee | query | No | Can be the name of a user. Pass in none for issues with no assigned user, and * for issues assigned to any user. |
| type | query | No | Can be the name of an issue type. If the string * is passed, issues with any type are accepted. If the string none i |
| creator | query | No | The user that created the issue. |
| mentioned | query | No | A user that's mentioned in the issue. |
| labels | query | No | A list of comma separated label names. Example: bug,ui,@high |
| sort | query | No | What to sort results by. |
| direction | query | No | The direction to sort the results by. |
| since | query | No | Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.or |
| per_page | query | No | The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.git |
| page | query | No | The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.gith |
Response Codes

200 Response
301 Moved permanently
404 Resource not found
422 Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.

data.name: List issue events for a repository
data.description:
Lists events for a repository.
Documentation: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/events
Quick Start:
- Set the Accept header to application/vnd.github+json (recommended).
- If accessing private repositories or more than public data, include a bearer token (see Authentication). For fine-grained tokens, the token must include repository "Issues" permission (read).
- Call: GET https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/events
Parameters Explained:
- Headers:
  - Accept (recommended): application/vnd.github+json.
  - Authorization (optional when accessing private resources): Bearer <TOKEN>.
  - X-GitHub-Api-Version (optional): version string such as 2026-03-10 (shown in examples).
- Path parameters:
  - owner (required): repository owner (case-insensitive string).
  - repo (required): repository name without .git (case-insensitive string).
- Query parameters:
  - per_page (integer, optional): Number of results per page (max 100). Default: 30.
  - page (integer, optional): Page number to fetch. Default: 1.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 200 OK: Successful response.
- 422 Validation failed or 422 endpoint has been spammed: Usually invalid query parameters or rate/abuse protections triggered — check request parameters and retry after a delay.
- Authorization issues: If you receive 401/403, ensure Authorization header is present and token has the required repository scope/permissions.
Edge Cases:
- This endpoint can be called without authentication for public repositories; to access private repository events you must provide a valid token with appropriate permissions.
- Some event fields (for example, commit_id, commit_url, or nested issue content) may be null or absent depending on event type.
- Pagination: results are paginated; use per_page and page to iterate through results and examine Link headers in responses for navigation.
Rate Limits & Constraints:
- Subject to GitHub REST API rate limits. For numeric limits and details (per authenticated vs unauthenticated requests), see the GitHub REST API Rate Limits documentation.

data.name: List issue comments for a repository
data.description:
List issue comments for a repository
You can use the REST API to list comments on issues and pull requests for a repository. Every pull request is an issue, but not every issue is a pull request.
By default, issue comments are ordered by ascending ID.
This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "Media types."

application/vnd.github.raw+json: Returns the raw markdown body. Response will include body. This is the default if you do not pass any specific media type.
application/vnd.github.text+json: Returns a text only representation of the markdown body. Response will include body_text.
application/vnd.github.html+json: Returns HTML rendered from the body's markdown. Response will include body_html.
application/vnd.github.full+json: Returns raw, text, and HTML representations. Response will include body, body_text, and body_html.

Parameters
| Name | In | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| owner | path | Yes | The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive. |
| repo | path | Yes | The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive. |
| sort | query | No | The property to sort the results by. |
| direction | query | No | Either asc or desc. Ignored without the sort parameter. |
| since | query | No | Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.or |
| per_page | query | No | The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.git |
| page | query | No | The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.gith |
Response Codes

200 Response
404 Resource not found
422 Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.

Documentation: https://docs.github.com/rest/issues/comments#list-issue-comments-for-a-repository

data.name: Get GitHub Actions permissions for a repository
data.description:
Get GitHub Actions permissions for a repository (shows whether Actions are enabled and allowed actions configuration).
Documentation: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/permissions
Quick Start:
- Authorization: token with repo scope (classic) or fine-grained token with repository Administration (read).
- GET https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions with Accept: application/vnd.github+json
Parameters Explained:
- owner (path, required): account owner of the repository.
- repo (path, required): repository name.
- Header accept: application/vnd.github+json recommended.
Common Errors & Fixes:
- 401/403: insufficient token or scope.
- 404: repository not found or lack of access.
Edge Cases:
- Fine-grained tokens supported: GitHub App user/installation tokens and fine-grained PATs with "Administration" repository permission (read).

Not supported: workflow runs, workflow creation, permission updates, issue management
